steps.what: Snap tails to the burned marks, fix sub-fascia, rakes.

benefits.value: 0.3 h saved on 8 fascia and rake boards (about CAD 14)
benefits.detail: Assumes 3.0 min per fascia and rake board measured and cut on site versus 1.0 min with a labelled, pre-cut part, at CAD 46.2/h loaded. Replace with your own time study.

benefits.value: 6.7% cut waste vs 10% typical order allowance
benefits.detail: Acucut 1D nester on this trade's 8 sticks: 8 boards, 36.58 m stock for 34.14 m of parts (bundle-window constrained runs add about 0.5 points). Conventional allowance 5 to 15% (BuildingScience). Difference about 4 bf, CAD 3 at CAD 700/MBF (estimate).

FMI puts rework at about 5% of construction spend and 48% of rework on poor communication or data. If labelled, sequenced, pre-checked parts prevent 15 to 30% of this trade's rework (estimate), callbacks fall by 0.75 to 1.50% of trade spend. On the NAHB reference home (US$428,215 build, 3.9% share = US$16,700) that is US$125 to US$251; not scaled to the 96 m2 sample.

cell_does: Cuts the sub-fascia with rafter tail centres burned (406 mm layout) and rakes with both plumb cuts.
Roofing takeoff from the model: 69.3 m2 = 7.5 squares.
cell_cannot: Cut shingles, membrane or metal panels.
app: Build: roof steps under fall protection.
summary: Sub-fascia with every rafter tail burned on, and rake boards with the 30.3 degree plumb cuts, so the eave line is straight and the drip edge goes on once.
highlight: Sub-fascia with 22 rafter tails burned on, rakes with 30.3 degree plumb cuts; 7.5 squares from the model.
routing: Acucut routing: the cell's nester groups this trade's parts by section and stock length, cuts them in bundle order (last-installed at the bottom), laser-burns the label, QR and every mark listed, and drops each bundle in its zone so the crew picks in install order.
